correctness.rationale: All 16-vertex graph adjacencies and 48 edges are constructed from definitions; for every one of 1128 pairs of edges, separator masks exactly encode the resolving quantifier. Exhaustive 16-choose-k scans below and at k=6 (Shrikhande) and k=5 (rook) agree with separate edge-distance-vector uniqueness checks, proving minimum sizes 6,5 and exact bases 736,576. Enumerated 192 and 1152 automorphisms saturate rigorously checked \(16\cdot12\) and \(16\cdot72\) upper bounds from neighborhoods with uniquely profiling nonneighbors, certifying full groups; orbit sizes sum to counts. Basis-exchange mask adjacency covers every legal swap and BFS proves both connected, with degree and edge totals cross-checked. Reproduce from verify_edge_metric.py in this exact package. No infinite extension or external audit.

value.rationale: The Shrikhande and 4x4 rook graphs are the classical nonisomorphic strongly regular (16,6,2,2) pair, where adjacency spectrum and local intersection parameters cannot distinguish them. An exact vertex-landmark requirement for edge localization separates them sharply (6 vs 5), while complete minimum-basis geometry reveals a seven-orbit, irregular exchange graph versus one-orbit, 13-regular behavior. This is a natural exact classification and motivated boundary on what strongly regular parameters determine, not a selected numerical slice; independently valuable even without a family-wide theorem.
